parts.gloss: to those with the great fault

words.gloss: to those with the great fault

literal: Modesty called good woman back will give to those of the not-cherished great fault called liquor.
translation: The virtuous maiden called Modesty will turn her back and depart from those who commit the undesirable, grave crime of drinking liquor.
modern: நாணம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் நல்ல பெண்மகள், கள் குடித்தல் என்னும் விரும்பத்தகாத பெரும் குற்றத்தைச் செய்பவர்களுக்குத் தன் முதுகைக் காட்டி விலகிப் போவாள்.
explanation: This couplet personifies modesty as a virtuous woman who abandons those who drink liquor. The poet describes drinking as an undesirable, grave vice (பேணா பெருங்குற்றம்) that strips a person of their dignity. When a person consumes alcohol, they lose their self-control and sense of shame, symbolized by the lady of Modesty turning her back (புறங்கொடுக்கும்) on them. Thus, the desire for liquor drives away one's innate decency and self-respect.
